messages.subject: facets, grouping, and freqpoly
parts:
The following example code is not giving me the desired output. I
thought the group would give ..count.. over just the specified group,
but I'm not seeing that. I'm sure this is an easy fix, i'm just
stumped.


histframe=data.frame(data=c(rnorm(10000,mean=75,sd=5),rnorm(400,mean=50,sd=2)),
site=c(replicate(5000,'A'),replicate(5000,'B'),
replicate(200,'A'),replicate(200,'B')),
res=c(replicate(5000,'H'),replicate(5000,'H'),
replicate(200,'L'),replicate(200,'L')) )

hist <- ggplot(histframe) +
facet_wrap(~site,ncol=2) + theme_bw() +
geom_freqpoly(aes(x=data,y=..count../
sum(..count..),colour=res,group=res),
binwidth=.15,linetype=1,width=.5) +
hist

messages.subject: RE: facets, grouping, and freqpoly
parts:
Hi McCreight,

not sure if this is what you want, but ..density.. seems to work (relative
frequencies?)

hist <- ggplot(histframe) +
facet_wrap(~site,ncol=2) + theme_bw() +

geom_freqpoly(aes(x=data, y=..density..,colour=res,group=res),
binwidth=.15,linetype=1,width=.5)
hist

Similar output with

hist <- ggplot(histframe) +
facet_wrap(~site,ncol=2) + theme_bw() +

geom_density(aes(x=data, colour=res),
binwidth=.15)
hist


hope this helps,
fenrando

y-axis upto about 5 and when i use ..density.. i get a range upto
about 3.5. Clearly something is not working as advertised, at least as
far as I understand it.

I'd like to give a repeatable example, but the actual data i'm working
with has about a half-million points. Maybe this has something to do
with it. Any thoughts would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks again,

James

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: facets, grouping, and freqpoly
parts:
> You know that would be really nice *IF* density gave me the units I
> expect. So this is really the cause of the original problem, ie why i
> choose to use ..count../sum(..count..) in the first place.

Or you could expect the right units ;) The density is count / width /
sum(abs(count), na.rm=TRUE) - i.e. it also takes into account the
width of the bars, and so will work for non-equal interval histograms.

> The problem is that when I use geom_density i get a range on the
> y-axis upto about 5 and when i use ..density.. i get a range upto
> about 3.5. Clearly something is not working as advertised, at least as
> far as I understand it.

Can you provide a small reproducible example? You won't necessarily
expect that the histogram and density to have the same range of
density (depending on bin width and bandwidth), but they should be
similar.

Hadley

messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: Re: facets, grouping, and freqpoly
parts: Hadley-
> Or you could expect the right units ;)
Actually, I couldnt agree with you more!

The density is count / width /
> sum(abs(count), na.rm=TRUE)  - i.e. it also takes into account the
> width of the bars, and so will work for non-equal interval histograms.

This is all I need. It just had not occurred to me that this was
normalized by the bin width. I was unable to infer this using only my
pea brain and the documentation. I'd advocate putting the formula in
with each variable produced by stat_bin so it's clearer what to
expect.

I've set y=(..density..)*binwidth to get what I want. We havent solved
the issue of why (..count..)/sum(..count..) dosent work properly, but
this is equivalent.

Much thanks for bearing with me.

James
